title: Measure how far the rows are from agreeing

blocks.text: A transit agency's maintenance LP came back `INFEASIBLE`. Before anyone hunts for the culprit row, the planners want one number: how far apart are the rows? Zero would mean the report was wrong; anything above zero is the least total amount by which the rows must be relaxed.

Write `total_violation(rows)` in `violation.py`. Each row is `(a, sense, b)`: a list of coefficients, `"<="` or `">="`, and a right-hand side. The decision variables are $`x_j \ge 0`$, one per coefficient. Build and solve, with GLOP, the phase-1 LP that gives every row $`r`$ an elastic variable $`v_r`$:
and return its optimal value, a float. This LP always has an optimum (any $`x`$ fits once the $`v_r`$ are large enough, and the sum cannot go below 0), so there is no other status to handle.

print("x + y <= 8, x >= 1, y >= 2:", round(total_violation([([1, 1], "<=", 8), ([1, 0], ">=", 1), ([0, 1], ">=", 2)]), 6))
print("x + y <= 8, x + y >= 13:", round(total_violation([([1, 1], "<=", 8), ([1, 1], ">=", 13)]), 6))
print("x >= 6, x <= 1, 3x <= 6:", round(total_violation([([1], ">=", 6), ([1], "<=", 1), ([3], "<=", 6)]), 6))

cases.says: rows some plan satisfies give a total stretch of 0
a cap of 30 and a floor of 34 on the same sum need a stretch of 4
a >= row is stretched by lowering its right-hand side, so it can absorb the gap itself
the decision variables keep their bounds x >= 0, so a row only negative values could meet must stretch

origin.section: Phase 1 Measures How Far the Rows Are From Agreeing, and Finds a First Vertex When They Do

concepts: an infeasible LP has no plan that meets every row, and INFEASIBLE is a proof of that
phase 1 gives every row an elastic variable and minimizes their sum: zero means feasible
